source.title: Dissecting Hessian: Understanding Common Structure of Hessian in Neural Networks
source.authors: Yikai Wu; Xingyu Zhu; Chenwei Wu; Annie Wang; Rong Ge

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; the supplied text includes the main paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Measures Hessian structure and eigenspace overlap in networks trained on natural and random labels, and reports PAC-Bayes classification errors and gaps. These results bear on the generalization versions, but do not apply the versions’ defining interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported classification test error and empirical generalization gap in the PAC-Bayes table, plus the separately reported Hessian overlap on natural and random-label datasets. Hessian values used to characterize structure are not themselves training-test gap measurements. Cited results from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The matched T-600/R-600 experiments report natural-label and random-label held-out performance for the same fully connected architecture on binary MNIST. They test V1's held-out contrast in a new setting, but do not establish nearly perfect random-label training fit. Hessian structure and improved PAC-Bayes bounds do not themselves test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose a decoupling conjecture explaining several layer-wise Hessian structures, prove results at initialization for a two-layer network, verify implications empirically more broadly, and use Hessian information to tighten PAC-Bayes bounds. They leave preservation of the theoretical properties throughout training open.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Hessian structure and PAC-Bayes bounds rather than testing the claim versions’ interventions; its main models use SGD, batch size 128, fixed learning rate 0.01 and 1000 epochs without momentum or weight decay, except where stated otherwise.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and label type alter the observed eigenspectrum behavior; batch normalization and zero-mean layer inputs reduce the rank-one input autocorrelation pattern and remove the overlap peak in reported settings. Hessian overlap also varies by layer and network.

fits_no_version.finding: A Hessian-informed posterior produces tighter PAC-Bayes bounds than the baseline posterior parameterization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligning posterior covariance with an approximate layer-wise Hessian eigenbasis can tighten optimized PAC-Bayes classification bounds.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-derived subspace overlap with the output-Hessian top eigenspace varies across layers, architectures and label conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A weight-derived heuristic approximates the top output-Hessian eigenspace with setting-dependent accuracy.

record.problems: The paper states that its theory applies only to initialization for a two-layer network and that maintenance of the property during training is open. The PAC-Bayes table does not provide training error, and the reported Hessian overlaps are not direct measures of the claim versions’ generalization outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No reported Hessian values used solely to describe spectral structure or validate the decoupling conjecture were extracted. Those appear across Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendices F–G; they do not measure a version’s named outcome. Table 8 rows are retained only as measurements relevant to the claim’s subject but do not provide direct V1 verdict evidence.

untested.parts: Nearly perfect training fit on fixed random labels; the full coexistence conjunction; matched random-label comparisons for architectures other than F-600; the original CIFAR-10/ImageNet architectures and recipes. Convergence to a local minimum does not establish zero training error.
Test error versus width beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Held-out effects of batch size under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout.
Association between magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and generalization gaps, including comparison against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

missing.what: Additional natural-label held-out result: T-600²¹⁰ has test error 0.0186. Like the other unpaired natural-label rows, it does not establish random-label memorization.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 calls TestEr. an empirical generalization gap, whereas Table 10 identifies the same quantities as test error. Without corresponding training errors, these values should not be treated as measured train–test gaps. Missing training-fit evidence is an untested component, not evidence against V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the random-label fit and held-out accuracy comparison for the same architectures and recipes described in V1, or the cited Inception/AlexNet results.

relationships.condition: Held-out component only: F-600 on binary MNIST with true versus random labels.
relationships.reason: R1 and R5 report errors 0.015 and 0.493 respectively, supporting the natural-label versus chance-level random-label held-out contrast; random-label training fit remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: The reported low natural-label error and approximately chance random-label error remain unverified, while random-label training fit was untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
